messages.subject: error when initializing chains
parts:
I have a model that is very slow to converge. I think it would help a lot if I give it starting points that are at least in the ballpark, but when I try using init I get an error: 
====
SAMPLING FOR MODEL 'ts_code' NOW (CHAIN 1).
Error in sampler$call_sampler(args_list[[i]]) : 
  Error during user-specified initialization:
y is not between the lower and upper bounds
error occurred during calling the sampler; sampling not done
====

I assumed, of course, that I was trying to specify some initialization values outside the lower= and upper= bounds that I had set for the various parameters, but I have checked carefully and I don't think that's the case. I thought perhaps I was specifying some arrays of parameters with the wrong number of elements, so I checked that too...and sure enough I had something wrong...but fixing it did not fix the problem. Or, maybe I didn't fix it, perhaps I have the form of some of the data structures wrong. I have some parameters that are defined as, for example:
vector <lower=-10, upper=10> [n_DayTimes] beta_TOD[2,n_weeks]
and I am setting initial values using 
beta_TOD = beta_TOD_est
where beta_TOD_est is defined in R as:
beta_TOD_est = array(0,dim=c(2,n_weeks,n_DayTimes))

Am I doing this right?

Also, yet one more thing to add to the list of possible improvements for the future, it sure would be nice if Stan told me which argument is causing the problem!

Phil

On Saturday, February 16, 2013 8:14:54 PM UTC-5, Phil Price wrote:
I do think it would be nice, in some future Stan release, to get an error message specifying the name, or the location in the init list, of the problematic parameter.  It would also be nice to be able to send in as many or as few init values as I want, rather than having to choose all or none.

Those would both be nice. But for !Windows, you can diagnose this problem with gdb if you have it installed. From a shell, do

R -d gdb --vanilla

to start R under gdb. At the gdb prompt do these two lines

catch throw
run

at which point you will be in the R environment. At the R prompt do,

library(rstan)
set_cppo("debug")

then source your script that causes the problem. When the error is thrown, you will see a gdb prompt again, at which point you can get a backtrace by executing

bt

and look at the output.

Be sure to do

library(rstan)
set_cppo("fast")

after you have fixed the problem.

Ben
